decision.chosen: Every successful capability invocation, regardless of mode (graph-amplified, sparse-mode, or even gap), MUST emit a graph-write describing what it did. In sparse-mode this takes the form of an EnrichmentTask queued on TaskState.enrichmentQueue (Intent + capabilityId + reason='sparse_mode_used' | 'graph_only_gap'), executed by the orchestrator between passes when budget permits. In graph-amplified mode the graph-write is implicit (the graph-first intent itself records to the graph). The matrix declares enrichOnFallback per capability (e.g. mutate.file.create -> graph.scan; navigate.symbol -> graph.scan; mutate.file.edit -> api.modify; search.ui -> ui.register). Enrichment is opportunistic, not blocking.

alternatives.option: Only graph-amplified mode writes to graph; sparse-mode is read-only
alternatives.rejected_because: Sparse installs would never bootstrap the graph; the architect would never improve on a project; contradicts user directive to 'evolve with time through edges and dreams'

alternatives.option: Manual scan_project on schedule, not driven by capability invocations
alternatives.rejected_because: Decouples enrichment from actual usage; the graph grows in directions the architect doesn't actually use

alternatives.option: Synchronous enrichment after each capability invocation
alternatives.rejected_because: Blocks the pass on graph writes; defeats sparse-mode parity with generic agents

expected: A project worked on with the architect for a week is measurably more graph-rich than one worked on for a day
Sparse installs converge on graph-amplified for the capabilities the user actually exercises
Generic-agent equivalent has no analogue — this is a structural advantage that compounds with project tenure
Slice 5 cards can show 'enrichment queued: graph.scan' as a pill
risks: Enrichment queue grows unbounded if orchestrator never drains — mitigated by Slice 7 verification + budget caps
Misclassified enrichOnFallback wastes graph-write budget — mitigated by per-capability review against §8 of the plan

guard_rails: Every capability that has a fallback path MUST declare an enrichOnFallback intent OR explicitly note 'no enrichment meaningful' in winRationale
Enrichment MUST NOT block the originating pass
EnrichmentTask reason MUST be one of 'sparse_mode_used' | 'graph_only_gap'
Orchestrator MUST eventually drain the enrichment queue (Slice 7 verifies)

decisions.title: Slice 7 — Verification planner is a frozen capability->verifications table; planVerifications is pure

context.problem: Without a frozen capability->verification table, verification logic spreads across imperative branches and the 'every code change should attempt relevant verification' goal becomes unauditable. Read-only capabilities would also waste budget on irrelevant build/test runs.
constraints: Table must cover every CapabilityId (TypeScript Record<CapabilityId, PlanEntry> exhaustiveness)
Verification capabilities (verify.*) map to NONE to prevent infinite recursion
planVerifications is pure: no I/O, no Date.now, no random
Failed mutations short-circuit to empty plan; classifier produces mutation_failed status

decision.chosen: VERIFICATION_PLAN_TABLE is a frozen Record<CapabilityId, PlanEntry> covering every Slice-6 CapabilityId exhaustively (TypeScript compile gate). planVerifications(capabilityId, mutationOutcome) is pure: returns empty plan for failed mutations and for read-only/env-IO capabilities; returns the table's entry otherwise. VERIFICATION_PERFORMED_BY maps each VerificationKind to its Slice-6 verifier capability so the orchestrator can route through Slice 6 selection without coupling planner to capability internals.

alternatives.option: Switch statement per CapabilityId in planner
alternatives.rejected_because: 42 capabilities -> 42 arms; impossible to audit against the plan §1 table

alternatives.option: Configurable per-project verification rules
alternatives.rejected_because: Premature; provider-neutral defaults must work first; per-project overrides can be additive later

alternatives.option: Always run all verifications regardless of capability
alternatives.rejected_because: Wastes budget on read-only operations; conflicts with token economy goal

expected: Adding a CapabilityId is a single table entry + one classifier branch (compile error otherwise)
Read-only operations skip verification entirely (token economy preserved)
Mutations always have type+build attempted (catches regressions immediately)
Markdown mutations route to lint not build (correct cost profile)
Graph mutations route to discipline+invariant (preserves graph invariants)
risks: Table grows stale if a capability changes verification needs (mitigated by ADR-164 same-commit guard rail extension)
Markdown projects without a markdown linter see 'verification_unavailable' (acceptable: surfaced as typed status, not a failure)

guard_rails: VERIFICATION_PLAN_TABLE MUST stay Object.freeze'd; no runtime mutation
Adding a CapabilityId requires updating VERIFICATION_PLAN_TABLE in the same commit
verify.* capabilities MUST map to NONE (no recursive verification)
planVerifications MUST stay pure (no I/O, no Date.now, no random)

decisions.title: Slice 7 — CompletionStatus is a closed 6-kind discriminated union with assertNeverStatus exhaustiveness

context.problem: Verification logic must enforce ADR-163's never-fall guarantee at runtime: a missing toolchain or a verification failure must produce a typed status, not an exception. Without a closed discriminated union, dispatch sites diverge and 'partial completion' creeps back as a silent half-state.
constraints: Status set is closed; new kinds require ADR + update of every dispatch site
verification_unavailable is a status, not an exception
classifyCompletion is pure (no I/O, no Date.now)
Exhaustiveness enforced by assertNeverStatus(s: never): never at every dispatch

decision.chosen: CompletionStatus is a closed 6-kind discriminated union: completed, completed_no_verification_needed, repair_recommended, blocked, failed_verification (reason: verification_unavailable), mutation_failed. assertNeverStatus(s: never): never is exported and used at every dispatch site so adding a kind without updating consumers is a compile error. classifyCompletion never throws on missing toolchain; it returns failed_verification with the missing kinds enumerated.

alternatives.option: Throw on missing toolchain instead of returning a status
alternatives.rejected_because: violates ADR-163 never-fall: a single missing toolchain would crash the whole pass and lose unrelated work

alternatives.option: Open status set with arbitrary string kinds
alternatives.rejected_because: loses exhaustiveness, makes card rendering and metrics aggregation a guessing game

alternatives.option: Boolean 'completed' flag plus optional reason
alternatives.rejected_because: loses the structured discriminator cards and metrics need; ambiguous about repair vs blocker vs unavailable

expected: Cards (Slice 5) can switch on .kind with TS exhaustiveness enforcement
Missing toolchain surfaces as a typed blocker the user can act on
Mutation failures are clearly distinguished from verification failures in metrics
Adding a 7th status requires touching every consumer (intentional friction)
risks: Adding new status kinds is high-friction (intentional); requires ADR amendment
assertNeverStatus only catches drift at compile time; tests need to exercise each kind to confirm runtime dispatch

guard_rails: Every switch on CompletionStatus.kind MUST end with assertNeverStatus(s)
classifyCompletion MUST NOT throw for missing toolchain (return failed_verification instead)
New CompletionStatus kinds MUST be added in the same commit as their ADR and all consumers
verification_unavailable's missingKinds array MUST be non-empty when this status is returned

decisions.title: Slice 7 — Repair loop is bounded (1 attempt per kind per task) and always a ContinuationNeed, never inline retry

context.problem: A failed verification needs a bounded recovery path that is observable to Slice 3's autonomy budget and Slice 5's cards. Inline retries hide cost and break ADR-154 (tool-name embedding). Unbounded repair loops eat budget and never surface a clean blocker.
constraints: Repair MUST be a continuation (Slice 3 ContinuationNeed), never an inline retry
ContinuationNeed.continuationPrompt MUST embed the verification tool name (ADR-154 enforced by createContinuationNeed)
Repair budget defaults to 1 per VerificationKind per task (overridable per call, not globally mutated)
planRepair is pure (no I/O, no Date.now, no random)

decision.chosen: planRepair is pure: input is (failedStep, repairAttemptsByKind, autonomyBudget, optional nonActionable). Default budget is DEFAULT_REPAIR_BUDGET_PER_KIND = 1 attempt per VerificationKind per task. Repair always emits a ContinuationNeed via createContinuationNeed (which enforces ADR-154 tool-name embedding); inline retry is forbidden. Output is a 3-arm discriminated union: repair_with_continuation, escalate_to_blocker (when budget or autonomy exhausted), skip_repair (when caller flags non_actionable).

alternatives.option: Inline retry of the failed verification tool
alternatives.rejected_because: loses Slice 3 budget accounting; the autonomy state machine never sees the retry; ADR-154 invariant becomes invisible

alternatives.option: Unbounded repair attempts
alternatives.rejected_because: trivial path to runaway loops; conflicts with token economy and Slice 3 stop conditions

alternatives.option: Repair budget shared across all kinds
alternatives.rejected_because: a flaky build alone could exhaust budget for all other kinds; per-kind isolation gives finer-grained signals

expected: At most 1 repair continuation per failed verification kind per task by default
Repair is observable in the autonomy budget view (continuationsRemaining decrements)
ADR-154 tool-name invariant is enforced at construction time (no silent drift)
Non-actionable failures produce a soft blocker, not a silent skip (user always sees the gap)
risks: Default of 1 repair may be too aggressive for flaky tests (mitigated by maxAttemptsPerKind override and nonActionable flag)
Per-kind counters add a small amount of state to TaskState (additive widening per ADR-151)

guard_rails: planRepair MUST NOT call createContinuationNeed without a tool name (createContinuationNeed throws)
Repair attempts MUST be tracked per VerificationKind, not globally
skip_repair MUST emit a soft Blocker (no silent verification skips)
Default budget changes require ADR amendment (do not silently increase)

decisions.title: Slice 7 — CompletionMetrics is a pure derivation from (outcomes, plans, classifications); no mutable counter store

context.problem: Cards (Slice 5) and the orchestrator both want completion counters, and v1 maintained mutable counter state at multiple sites that drifted. Without a single derivation function, replaying a pass for diagnosis produces different numbers than the original.
constraints: computeMetrics is pure: same input -> same output (no Date.now, no random, no I/O)
Every metric field is derivable from canonical arrays (outcomes, plans, classifications); no parallel mutable store
STATUS_RANK ordering is the single source of truth for finalStatus aggregation
Metric counters are non-negative integers

decision.chosen: computeMetrics(input) is a pure function that derives CompletionMetrics from (outcomes, capabilityPlans, verificationPlans, classifications, priorRepairAttemptsByKind, enrichmentTasksDrained). All counters are computed by scanning the canonical event/plan arrays — no parallel mutable counter store. finalStatus is the worst-case classification rank across the pass (mutation_failed > failed_verification > blocked > repair_recommended > completed_no_verification_needed > completed). enrichmentTasksDrained is supplied by the orchestrator (it owns the queue), but every other field is locally derivable.

alternatives.option: Counters as mutable fields incremented at side-effect sites
alternatives.rejected_because: double-counting bugs are the v1 metrics failure mode; mutable counters drift from the source of truth

alternatives.option: Compute metrics inside the orchestrator only
alternatives.rejected_because: couples cards (Slice 5) to orchestrator internals; cards should consume a typed result instead

alternatives.option: Persist metrics to disk per pass
alternatives.rejected_because: premature; cards consume in-memory; persistence can be added without changing the derivation function

expected: Cards (Slice 5) render counters by calling computeMetrics; no parallel state to keep in sync
Replaying a pass's outcomes always produces identical metrics (testable, deterministic)
Adding a new metric field is a pure additive change to computeMetrics
finalStatus aggregation is consistent across all consumers (single STATUS_RANK table)
risks: enrichmentTasksDrained must be supplied externally (orchestrator owns the drain loop); slight asymmetry vs other fields
Re-deriving on every render has small CPU cost (acceptable: O(n) over a single pass's outcomes)

guard_rails: computeMetrics MUST NOT read from disk, network, or clocks
STATUS_RANK MUST be updated in the same commit as any new CompletionStatus kind
New metric fields MUST be derivable from existing inputs OR added as explicit input parameters
TaskState additions for metrics MUST be additive widening only (ADR-151 preserved)

decisions.title: Architect orchestrator binds to ProjectGraphReader/Recorder, not DreamGraph

context.problem: The Architect v2 orchestrator (Slice 8A.1) is the seam through which every later sub-slice will fetch graph context (8A.3) and persist cognition (8A.4). If the orchestrator or ContextBuilder imports mcp_dreamgraph_* directly, DreamGraph's MCP shape becomes the de-facto required ontology for the Architect. That violates the slice's "graph-native, not DreamGraph-native" framing: sparse/no-graph projects, alternative graph backends (LSP-derived, Sourcegraph, custom AST graphs), and future cognition stores would all be second-class. The orchestrator must depend only on a project-graph abstraction; DreamGraph is one adapter behind it.
constraints: Strict isolation (ADR-140) extended: no architect-v2 module outside an explicit adapters/ folder may import mcp_dreamgraph_*.
Ports must be narrow enough that an LSP-only or filesystem-only adapter is implementable without stubs returning fake graph nodes.
Reader returns an opaque ProjectSubgraph; the orchestrator does not introspect its internals beyond what ContextBuilder uses to assemble a ContextEnvelope.
Recorder methods are async and idempotent on identity (re-recording the same card id is a no-op or upsert; never duplicates).
Sparse/no-graph mode is a first-class operating mode, not an error path.

decision.chosen: Define two narrow ports in 8A.1 — ProjectGraphReader (richness signal, subgraph retrieval, neighbors) and ProjectGraphRecorder (record cards, decisions, outcomes, continuations) — and add them to OrchestratorPorts. The orchestrator, ContextBuilder, PromptComposer, and Memory layers consume only these ports. The DreamGraph adapter is implemented in 8A.3 behind the Reader port and in 8A.4 behind the Recorder port; nothing in architect-v2/orchestrator/, architect-v2/context/, architect-v2/prompts/, or architect-v2/memory/ (outside an explicit */adapters/dreamgraph/ subfolder) may import mcp_dreamgraph_*. Sparse/no-graph projects receive top-tier behavior via filesystem/runtime/LSP context reconstruction; resulting cognition is still recorded through the Recorder when one is wired.

alternatives.option: Continue with no abstraction; ContextBuilder calls mcp_dreamgraph_* directly.
alternatives.rejected_because: Bakes DreamGraph's schema into the Architect; no path to alternative backends; sparse projects degrade to broken instead of degraded-but-functional.

alternatives.option: Single ProjectGraphReader port (read-only); persist via DreamGraph directly from Memory.
alternatives.rejected_because: Asymmetric — recording is where ontology coupling is strongest (cards, ADRs, continuations all become DreamGraph entity types). Reader without Recorder leaks the schema on the write path.

alternatives.option: Defer the abstraction until after 10.0 cutover; ship 8A.3 against mcp_dreamgraph_* and refactor later.
alternatives.rejected_because: Slice 8A.3 is the exact place the leak crystallizes; refactoring after cutover means rewriting the Architect's hottest path under load.

expected: 8A.3 ships ContextBuilder + a DreamGraph Reader adapter side-by-side; the Reader interface, not the adapter, is what ContextBuilder depends on.
8A.4 ships Memory + a DreamGraph Recorder adapter; an in-memory Recorder is trivial for tests.
The Architect can be lifted into a non-DreamGraph host (or run before DreamGraph has indexed anything) without changing orchestrator code.
Density measurement (Slice 6) is fed by Reader.getRichnessSignal, not by direct dream://graph reads.
Existing cognition stores keep working; they are written through the Recorder adapter.
risks: Port surface drifts smaller than ContextBuilder needs, forcing a leaky 'getRaw' escape hatch. Mitigation: 8A.3 may extend the port additively but each addition is justified in its slice plan.
Recorder becomes a thin pass-through with little value over direct writes. Mitigation: Recorder owns identity normalization (card ids → graph node ids) which is real ontology work, not a wrapper.
Performance: extra indirection on every context fetch. Mitigation: ports are async and the adapter can batch/cache freely; the orchestrator does not assume locality.

guard_rails: Lint/CI rule (added in Slice 8B): grep for mcp_dreamgraph_ outside architect-v2/**/adapters/dreamgraph/** fails the build.
ProjectGraphReader and ProjectGraphRecorder method signatures are frozen by this ADR; widening is allowed (additive ADR-151 style), narrowing requires an amending ADR.
No port method returns a DreamGraph-specific type. ProjectGraphNode/Edge/Subgraph are defined in architect-v2 and intentionally narrower than DreamGraph's internal model.

Sparse-mode behavior is verified by a test that runs the orchestrator with a NullProjectGraphReader (always returns 'absent' richness) and a NullProjectGraphRecorder (no-op writes) and still produces a useful pass.

decisions.title: runPass is pure-shaped over OrchestratorPorts; no direct I/O

context.problem: The orchestrator pass loop is the hottest path in the Architect. If runPass performs I/O directly, every later sub-slice has to mock the runtime to test against it, and replacing any subsystem means editing the orchestrator. v1 fell into exactly this trap.
constraints: No top-level imports in loop.ts other than architect-v2 sibling modules.
Every async boundary in runPass is a port method call. No raw setTimeout, no Date.now (use ClockPort), no console.* (logging is a future port if needed).
runPass returns a PassResult; it never throws for predictable failure modes — those become CompletionStatus values and BlockerCard / CompletionCard outputs.
OrchestratorPorts is the only parameter shape that may grow; widening is allowed (additive ADR-151 style), removal/rename requires an amending ADR.

decision.chosen: runPass is a pure-shaped async function over an injected OrchestratorPorts bag. All effects (context build, prompt compose, provider call, tool execution, persistence, graph reads, graph recording, time) go through one of: ContextBuilderPort, PromptComposerPort, ExecutorPort, MemoryPort, ProjectGraphReader, ProjectGraphRecorder, ClockPort. The loop never imports vscode, fs, http, or mcp_* modules. Tests assemble runPass from in-memory fakes; production assembles from real adapters wired by the extension activate function (Slice 8A.5).

alternatives.option: Allow runPass to import vscode/fs/http directly for 'small' I/O.
alternatives.rejected_because: Every exception trains the next reader that exceptions are fine; tests then need real fakes for the 'small' I/O too.

alternatives.option: Pass a single mega-port that bundles every effect.
alternatives.rejected_because: Hides dependency surface; every consumer would import the union.

alternatives.option: Use module-level singletons to avoid passing ports.
alternatives.rejected_because: Same global-state failure mode v1 had; impossible to run two orchestrator instances with different providers in the same process.

expected: Sub-slices 8A.2–8A.5 can be implemented in any order — each delivers one port adapter runPass already calls.
Unit testing runPass is trivial: assemble all ports as in-memory fakes and assert on PassResult.
The Architect can be embedded in a non-VS Code host by swapping adapter implementations.
Refactors of any single subsystem cannot break the orchestrator: the port contract is the firewall.
risks: A future contributor adds a 'small' direct import for convenience. Mitigation: build-time guard rail.
Port count grows unbounded. Mitigation: each new port requires its own justification.
Determinism leaks via Math.random for card ids. Mitigation: future ADR may introduce an IdGenerator port.

guard_rails: Build-time check (Slice 8B): grep that fails if loop.ts imports anything matching /^(vscode|fs|node:|http|mcp_)/.
Verification harness: a NullPorts fixture must drive at least one full pass to a terminal status without throwing.
Each new port method requires a one-line justification in the sub-slice plan that introduces it.

decisions.title: Sparse / no-graph operation is a first-class mode via Null ports

context.problem: If the orchestrator's behavior degrades to 'broken' or 'mostly empty' when no graph backend is wired, the Architect becomes useless for day-1 installs, for projects DreamGraph hasn't indexed yet, and for hosts that don't run DreamGraph at all. The 'graph-native' framing must not become 'graph-required'.
constraints: NullProjectGraphReader and NullProjectGraphRecorder live in orchestrator/project-graph.ts and MUST remain importable by tests without pulling in any backend.

ContextBuilder (8A.3) MUST produce a non-empty, useful ContextEnvelope when Reader returns NULL_PROJECT_SUBGRAPH — by falling back to filesystem/runtime/LSP signals — not a near-empty 'no graph available' envelope.
BlockerCards must NEVER cite 'graph not wired' as a blocker reason. The graph not being wired is not a failure.

decision.chosen: Sparse / no-graph operation is a first-class supported mode. The orchestrator wires NullProjectGraphReader (returns 'absent' richness, empty subgraphs) and NullProjectGraphRecorder (no-op writes) by default. runPass executes the same sequence regardless of backend presence: density measurement returns 'absent' \u2192 Slice 6 sparse-mode kicks in \u2192 ContextBuilder reconstructs context from filesystem/runtime/LSP signals \u2192 the user gets a useful pass. When a real Reader and Recorder are wired (e.g. the DreamGraph adapter in 8A.3/8A.4), the same loop produces graph-amplified passes. Cards are still emitted in sparse mode; they are simply not durably indexed when the Recorder is the null implementation.

alternatives.option: Throw / surface a 'graph backend missing' blocker when no Reader is wired.
alternatives.rejected_because: Punishes the user for the host's setup choice; turns sparse-mode (a designed operating mode) into an error.

alternatives.option: Auto-detect 'no graph' and switch to a different code path inside runPass.
alternatives.rejected_because: Branching on backend presence is exactly the coupling ADR-171 forbids; the loop must look identical regardless of who's behind the port.

alternatives.option: Refuse to run without a Recorder; force every host to wire one.
alternatives.rejected_because: Defeats the point of having an Architect that works on day 1 in any project.

expected: Day-1 install in any project (no DreamGraph indexing, no prior cards) yields a working Architect with reduced-but-real cognition.
Unit tests of the orchestrator can use the null ports directly without scaffolding a backend.
The DreamGraph adapter (8A.3/8A.4) becomes one optional enhancement among many possible backends, not a precondition for the Architect to function.
risks: Sparse-mode quality silently regresses because nobody tests it. Mitigation: dedicated NullPorts test in the verification harness.

ContextBuilder's sparse-mode path becomes a second implementation of context assembly, drifting from the graph-mode path. Mitigation: same ContextBuilder consumes the same Reader port; only the *content* of the subgraph changes.

guard_rails: A test (added in 8A.3 or 8A.4) drives a full pass with NullProjectGraphReader + NullProjectGraphRecorder and asserts the resulting PassResult contains at least one Card and a non-error CompletionStatus.
ContextBuilder sub-slice plan must explicitly enumerate its sparse-mode signal sources (filesystem walk, LSP queries, runtime probes, recent diagnostics).

decisions.title: PromptComposer declares context requirements; ContextAssembler fulfills

context.problem: ADR-171 + Slice 8A.2 invariant force the composer to be passive (no graph reads, no MCP). But a passive composer that only renders whatever the assembler chose creates a knowledge-gap: only the prompt template knows what *kinds* of context this particular pass actually needs (architectural decisions? unresolved blockers? prior failed attempts? ADR lineage?). If the assembler has to guess, it either over-fetches (wastes the window) or under-fetches (silently degrades the prompt). We need a way for the composer to *declare* its needs without *performing* retrieval.
constraints: composer.ts and requirements.ts MUST NOT import from execution/, MCP, vscode, fs, http, or ProjectGraphReader.
ContextRequirementManifest is a plain data structure (frozen). No callbacks, no thunks, no promises inside it.
ContextBuilderPort.buildContext receives the manifest as advisory input; the assembler MAY satisfy fewer than requested but MUST NOT fetch beyond declared kinds without an ADR amendment.
The composer MUST tolerate any envelope shape the assembler returns — missing requested kinds is not an error.
declareContextRequirements is pure: same inputs → same output, no clock, no randomness, no I/O.

decision.chosen: Two-step composer/assembler contract. The PromptComposer exposes a pure function declareContextRequirements(input) -> ContextRequirementManifest *in addition to* composePrompt. The orchestrator calls declareContextRequirements first, passes the manifest to ContextBuilderPort.buildContext, then calls composePrompt with the resulting ContextEnvelope. The composer stays passive about retrieval (no graph reads, no MCP calls, no I/O); it only declares what it would *like* to see. The assembler/RelevanceEngine remains the only cognition site: it interprets the manifest, ranks, fetches, trims, and emits the envelope. If a requirement cannot be satisfied (sparse mode, no graph), the assembler still emits an envelope and notes the unmet requirements via section provenance; the composer renders what it gets without retrying.

alternatives.option: Composer also retrieves graph data when it spots a gap.
alternatives.rejected_because: Smears cognition across two layers; tests need a graph to render a prompt; sparse-mode behavior depends on which layer ran first.

alternatives.option: Assembler guesses what each capability needs.
alternatives.rejected_because: Couples the assembler to every prompt template; adding a new capability touches both layers; the knowledge of 'what this prompt needs' belongs with the prompt.

alternatives.option: Static per-capability requirement tables owned by Slice 6.
alternatives.rejected_because: Requirements depend on the *user intent* and *continuation state*, not just the capability id. A pure table can't see those.

alternatives.option: Skip the manifest; let composer accept a richer envelope shape that already includes everything possibly needed.
alternatives.rejected_because: Forces the assembler to over-fetch on every pass; defeats budget discipline; loses the very signal the assembler needs to rank.

expected: Adding a new prompt template means editing the composer only — it declares its needs and the assembler already knows how to fulfill the supported kinds.
Adding a new retrieval source (e.g. test-history backend) means editing the assembler only — it learns to satisfy more requirement kinds, no composer change.
Tests can golden-file both layers independently: declareContextRequirements is pure; the assembler is tested with a fake reader; the composer is tested with a hand-built envelope.
Token budgets become declarative: composer says 'medium' for ADR lineage, assembler decides what 'medium' means against the active provider window.
risks: Manifest taxonomy bloats. Mitigation: requirement kinds are an enum union; adding a kind requires ADR.
Composer 'declares everything' to be safe, defeating budget discipline. Mitigation: golden-file tests assert minimal requirement sets per template; reviewer flag.
Assembler silently ignores half the manifest. Mitigation: assembler must mark unmet requirements in envelope section provenance (added in 8A.3); a metrics check could surface chronic mismatches.

guard_rails: Build-time check (Slice 8B): grep that fails if prompts/*.ts imports anything matching /^(vscode|fs|node:|http|mcp_)/ OR imports from ../execution/ or ../orchestrator/project-graph (composer must not see ProjectGraphReader at all).
Test (8A.3): assembler ignoring the manifest entirely (returns NULL_PROJECT_SUBGRAPH-derived envelope) must still produce a renderable prompt.
Test (8A.2): declareContextRequirements called twice with identical input must return deeply-equal manifests.

decisions.title: ContextBuilder is the RelevanceEngine; manifest-driven retrieval with graceful sparse-fallback

context.problem: The composer declares what context it wants (ADR-174). The orchestrator wires graph access through ProjectGraphReader (ADR-171) and graph-absent operation as first-class (ADR-173). Something has to *fulfill* the composer's manifest \u2014 deciding which requirement gets which signal source, how much of the window each gets, and what to do when the requested kind cannot be satisfied. That something is the ContextBuilder/RelevanceEngine. If its design is unclear, every requirement kind grows a bespoke retrieval path and sparse-mode becomes an afterthought.
constraints: context/*.ts MUST NOT import mcp_dreamgraph_*; only orchestrator/adapters/dreamgraph/** may.
ContextBuilder is pure-shaped over ports: ProjectGraphReader, FallbackSignalProvider, ClockPort. No vscode/fs/http/MCP imports in context/.
The builder MUST tolerate any subset of requirements (including empty manifest) and produce a renderable envelope.
FallbackSignalProvider methods MUST be safe to call when no workspace is open (return empty arrays, never throw).
SectionProvenance is additive on ContextSection (optional field) per ADR-151 widening rules.
Unmet requirements MUST be recorded; silent omission is a violation.

decision.chosen: ContextBuilder is the single RelevanceEngine site. It interprets the ContextRequirementManifest declared by the composer (ADR-174), allocates a per-requirement token slice from the provider window (priority-weighted with budget hint scaling), and dispatches each requirement to one of two signal sources: ProjectGraphReader for graph-shaped kinds (architectural_decisions, adr_lineage, unresolved_blockers, prior_failed_attempts, graph_neighborhood) or FallbackSignalProvider for non-graph kinds (file_excerpts, recent_history, runtime_diagnostics, environment_state). When the reader reports richness 'sparse' or 'absent' for a requested graph kind, the builder transparently retries the same requirement against FallbackSignalProvider \u2014 no separate sparse-mode code path. Each emitted ContextSection carries SectionProvenance recording (a) which requirement it answered, (b) which source served it, and (c) whether it represents a fallback substitution. Unmet requirements are recorded as zero-content provenance entries so the composer/audit can see what was asked for and not delivered. The builder never throws on missing data; it always returns a valid envelope.

alternatives.option: Treat sparse mode as a separate code path inside the builder ('if richness === absent { ... } else { ... }').
alternatives.rejected_because: Branching on backend presence is exactly the coupling ADR-171 forbids; both modes must run the same plan, only with different signal sources answering.

alternatives.option: Have the builder fail when a requirement cannot be satisfied at all.
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-173 mandates sparse mode is first-class; failure here would propagate as a blocker card and degrade UX in any unindexed project.

alternatives.option: Let the builder call mcp_dreamgraph_* directly for graph reads to skip the adapter layer.
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-171 invariant; the builder must only see the ProjectGraphReader port.

alternatives.option: Drop SectionProvenance and let the composer infer unmet requirements from missing sections.
alternatives.rejected_because: Inference is fragile (some kinds legitimately produce no section); explicit provenance keeps the audit trail and enables metrics on chronic mismatches.

expected: Day-1 install with no graph indexed produces useful context via filesystem + diagnostics + environment fallback.
Adding a new requirement kind requires (a) declare in composer, (b) dispatch case in builder — no other site changes.
Adding a new signal source means implementing FallbackSignalProvider (or a new port) and wiring it; the builder's dispatch table grows by one row.
Cognition recorded back to the graph (via ProjectGraphRecorder, already wired in 8A.1 finalize) feeds future passes — the loop closes itself.
risks: Provenance noise crowds the envelope. Mitigation: provenance is optional on ContextSection; assembler may set it only on actually-emitted sections and collect unmet entries in a side-channel field on the envelope.
Token allocation algorithm becomes adhoc and untestable. Mitigation: allocation is one pure function (allocateBudget) with golden-file tests in 8A.5.
Fallback substitution silently masks a graph backend regression. Mitigation: SectionProvenance includes a 'fallbackReason' when substitution occurs; metrics can surface fallback rates.

guard_rails: Build-time check (Slice 8B): grep that fails if context/*.ts imports anything matching /^(vscode|fs|node:|http|mcp_)/ OR imports from orchestrator/adapters/dreamgraph/.
Test (8A.3): builder with NullProjectGraphReader + NullFallbackSignalProvider produces a non-throwing envelope; every manifest requirement appears in section provenance (satisfied or unmet).
Test (8A.3): builder with NullProjectGraphReader + a fake FallbackSignalProvider returning data produces sections with provenance.source === 'fallback' for graph kinds.

decisions.title: ContextBuilder routes requirements to graph or fallback sources with provenance

context.problem: ADR-174 split prompt assembly into 'composer declares' and 'assembler fulfills'. But declaring is cheap; *fulfilling* must work in every realistic project state \u2014 fully indexed, partially indexed, sparse, and not indexed at all. A naive assembler that just queries the graph degrades to 'empty prompt' in sparse mode (ADR-173) and silently loses provenance about why a section was missing.
constraints: FallbackSignalProvider methods MUST be safe to call when no workspace is open — return empty results, never throw. NullFallbackSignalProvider satisfies this trivially.
Every ContextSection emitted by DefaultContextBuilder MUST carry provenance.
Sections produced via fallback for a graph-shaped requirement MUST set provenance.fallbackReason to one of {graph_sparse, graph_absent, graph_error}.
ContextEnvelope.unmetRequirements MUST be populated for every requirement the builder could not satisfy.
FallbackSignalProvider lives in context/ and MUST NOT import from orchestrator/project-graph (no graph types leak into the fallback path).

decision.chosen: Two-source assembler with provenance. DefaultContextBuilder routes each declared requirement to one of two sources: ProjectGraphReader for graph-shaped kinds (architectural_decisions, adr_lineage, unresolved_blockers, prior_failed_attempts, graph_neighborhood) and a new FallbackSignalProvider port for non-graph kinds (file_excerpts, recent_history, runtime_diagnostics, environment_state). When the graph reader reports 'sparse' or 'absent' richness for a graph-shaped requirement, the builder transparently substitutes the FallbackSignalProvider (shallow project walk + file excerpts of any anchors) and stamps the section with provenance recording the fallback reason. Every emitted ContextSection carries SectionProvenance {requirementKind, signalSource, fallbackReason?}. Requirements the assembler could not satisfy are listed in ContextEnvelope.unmetRequirements with a typed reason. The composer renders whatever it gets without retry.

alternatives.option: Hard-fail when graph is sparse — surface a BlockerCard.
alternatives.rejected_because: Punishes day-1 installs and projects not yet indexed; sparse-mode is a designed mode (ADR-173).

alternatives.option: Have the composer pick a different prompt template when graph is sparse.
alternatives.rejected_because: Couples cognition to rendering and forces the composer to know graph state — violates ADR-174.

alternatives.option: Single mega-port that bundles graph + filesystem + diagnostics.
alternatives.rejected_because: Hides where each signal came from; provenance unrecoverable; tests cannot stub one source without the other.

alternatives.option: Fall back silently with no provenance.
alternatives.rejected_because: Composer/audit cannot distinguish 'graph-amplified context' from 'shallow filesystem walk'; metrics get noisy.

expected: Day-1 installs (no graph indexed) get useful context via filesystem + diagnostics; the same prompt template runs.
When the graph is later populated, the same builder returns graph-amplified sections with no code change in composer or orchestrator.
Audit + future metrics can compute 'graph hit rate' per requirement kind directly from provenance.
Tests for the builder need only stub two ports (graph reader + fallback) to exercise every code path.
risks: Two source paths drift in capability over time. Mitigation: same DefaultContextBuilder dispatches to both; tests cover both with the same fixture set.
Provenance bloats envelope size. Mitigation: provenance is a small fixed-shape record (3 strings); negligible compared to content.
Fallback for graph-shaped requirements becomes the default because graph stays sparse. Mitigation: provenance is observable; future metrics surface chronic fallback rates.

guard_rails: Test (8A.5 or earlier): assembler called with NullProjectGraphReader + NullFallbackSignalProvider must return a non-throwing envelope with sections.length === 0 and unmetRequirements.length === manifest.requirements.length.
Build-time check (Slice 8B): grep that fails if context/*.ts imports from /^(vscode|fs|node:|http|mcp_)/ — the builder is a pure dispatcher; transport adapters live under orchestrator/adapters/.
Provenance assertion: a unit test reads every emitted section in a representative envelope and asserts provenance is set.

decisions.title: MemoryPort + ContextDiscoveryRecorder split incidental from deliberate cognition

context.problem: 8A.3 closed with the assembler reading from two sources (graph + fallback) and emitting provenance, but two pieces of cognition were still implicit: (a) Architect TaskState had no durable home so a VS Code reload erased the running task, and (b) per the user invariant 'all discovered cognition is still recorded back to graph', incidental artifacts surfaced by the assembler (file URIs read via fallback, graph nodes referenced by retrieval) had nowhere to land. The orchestrator's existing ProjectGraphRecorder writes deliberate cognition only (cards, decisions, outcomes, continuations) and is owned by finalize(), not by the assembler.
constraints: DefaultContextBuilder MUST NOT block on discoveryRecorder — it is fire-and-forget (void safeCall(...)).
ContextDiscoveryRecorder.recordDiscoveries MUST NOT throw; adapters wrap transport in try/catch.
DefaultMemoryAdapter MUST cap PassLog history (default 200 entries) to keep workspaceState bounded.
MemoryPort writes structural-clone-safe values only — plain objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans (vscode.Memento requirement).
ContextDiscoveryRecorder lives in context/ and MUST NOT import from orchestrator/project-graph (no DecisionRecord/OutcomeRecord types leak into the discovery path).

decision.chosen: Two new ports land in 8A.4. (1) MemoryPort gets a DefaultMemoryAdapter backed by a KeyValueStore seam (vscode.Memento-shaped); InMemoryKeyValueStore covers tests; NullMemoryPort covers dry-runs. PassLog history is bounded (default 200 entries) so workspace state never grows unbounded. (2) A NEW narrow port ContextDiscoveryRecorder is owned by the assembler (context/) and called by DefaultContextBuilder when assembly produces concrete artifact references (file URIs from fallback excerpts/walk, graph node URIs from retrieved subgraphs). The builder calls recordDiscoveries fire-and-forget at the end of assembly; failures are swallowed. The DreamGraph adapter (orchestrator/adapters/dreamgraph/recorder.ts) implements BOTH ProjectGraphRecorder AND ContextDiscoveryRecorder against the McpClient seam, batching discoveries into wire_links calls with relation 'context_touched_via_fallback' or 'context_referenced'. Keeping the two recorder ports separate enforces that incidental cognition cannot accidentally synthesize decisions and deliberate cognition cannot accidentally write incidental data without the orchestrator's consent.

alternatives.option: Have ContextBuilder call ProjectGraphRecorder directly with synthetic OutcomeRecords.
alternatives.rejected_because: Conflates incidental reads with deliberate writes; the orchestrator's audit log would fill with synthetic outcomes that did not correspond to executor invocations.

alternatives.option: Defer all write-back to the orchestrator's finalize() step using touched-file metadata pulled out of the envelope.
alternatives.rejected_because: Loses the via=fallback distinction (so the graph cannot promote candidate edges to validated edges later) and forces the orchestrator to know envelope internals.

alternatives.option: Persist memory directly to the filesystem from the orchestrator.
alternatives.rejected_because: Couples architect-v2 to a specific persistence transport and makes the test harness do disk I/O. The KeyValueStore seam matches vscode.Memento exactly so the host wiring is a one-line bind.

expected: Architect tasks survive VS Code reload (TaskState + bounded PassLog history persisted via MemoryPort).
Every assembled context envelope produces an audit trail in the graph: which task touched which artifacts via which path (graph vs fallback), enabling future candidate-edge promotion.
The DreamGraph adapter is the single place mcp_dreamgraph_* tool names appear; reader + recorder + discovery recorder all share one McpClient transport seam.
8A.5 host wiring becomes mechanical: bind KeyValueStore to ExtensionContext.workspaceState, bind McpClient to the real MCP transport.
risks: Discovery recorder failures are silent. Mitigation: adapter has logErrors flag for tests; fire-and-forget is intentional so reads never block.
Bounded PassLog history loses long-tail audit. Mitigation: durable graph still has the per-pass cards/decisions/outcomes; PassLog is only the orchestrator's local index.
wire_links call shape may not match what the DreamGraph server expects. Mitigation: the adapter is the only place that knows MCP shapes; an integration test in 8A.5 will exercise it end-to-end.

guard_rails: Test (8A.5 or 8B): DefaultContextBuilder constructed with NullContextDiscoveryRecorder must never throw even when assembly produces hundreds of discoveries.
Test: DefaultMemoryAdapter.appendPassLog called > maxPassLogEntries times must keep array length === maxPassLogEntries (oldest dropped).
Test: DreamGraphRecorderAdapter.recordDiscoveries with empty list must not call McpClient at all.
Build-time check (Slice 8B): grep that fails if context/discovery-recorder.ts imports from orchestrator/project-graph or anywhere else outside prompts/requirements + own module.

decisions.title: Architect-v2 host wiring is a single createArchitectHost factory

context.problem: 8A.1\u20138A.4 produced the orchestrator loop, composer, builder, fallback provider, memory adapter, and DreamGraph reader+recorder adapter. None of them are wired together. The v10.0.0 atomic cutover commit needs to replace the v1 Architect entry point in extension.ts with a single call against v2; without a host wiring module the cutover diff would have to know every port and adapter, defeating ADR-140's parallel-folder isolation. Additionally the builder's effectiveWindow() still returned a hard-coded 16k value; the provider's actual model window must thread through every pass.
constraints: createArchitectHost MUST resolve the model window via resolveDefaultModel exactly once per host instance; per-pass model resolution is forbidden (it would re-list models on every pass).
Every port the factory cannot construct because a dependency is missing MUST default to its Null implementation; the factory MUST NOT throw merely because optional wiring is absent.
When mcpClient is supplied, the same DreamGraphRecorderAdapter instance MUST satisfy BOTH the ProjectGraphRecorder and ContextDiscoveryRecorder ports (ADR-177's split is at the type level only).
host/ MUST NOT import from extension.ts, vscode, fs, http, or any v1 path — it composes ports from architect-v2 modules only.
windowTokensOverride exists only for intentional degradation (small-context dry runs, tests). Production callers leave it unset.

decision.chosen: A new architect-v2/host/ module exports `createArchitectHost(options)` returning `{ providerProfile, windowTokens, ports, runPass }`. The factory: (1) calls resolveDefaultModel(providerId) ONCE and caches model.contextWindow as the authoritative window for every subsequent pass; (2) substitutes Null implementations for any unwired port (MemoryPort -> NullMemoryPort when no workspaceState; ProjectGraphReader/Recorder -> Null* when no McpClient; FallbackSignalProvider -> NullFallbackSignalProvider when none supplied) so sparse-mode is the default rather than a special case; (3) when an McpClient is wired, BOTH the ProjectGraphRecorder slot and the ContextDiscoveryRecorder slot get the same DreamGraphRecorderAdapter instance \u2014 ADR-177's two-port split is preserved at the type level while sharing one transport at runtime; (4) returns a `runPass(taskState, userIntent)` closure that threads the resolved windowTokens through every RunPassInput. extension.ts is unchanged today; the v10.0.0 cutover commit replaces the v1 entry call with `host.runPass(...)`. All other modules untouched.

alternatives.option: Wire ports inline in extension.ts.
alternatives.rejected_because: Extension.ts would have to know every architect-v2 port and adapter; the cutover commit becomes a sprawling diff and any future port addition forces extension.ts churn.

alternatives.option: Make every port mandatory.
alternatives.rejected_because: Defeats sparse-mode (ADR-173). The host has to keep working when the workspace has no MCP server, no graph, and no fallback provider — day-1 install.

alternatives.option: Resolve the model window inside the builder on every pass.
alternatives.rejected_because: Resolving requires async listModels(); doing it per-pass adds a network call to every prompt. Resolve once at host construction; thread the number through every pass.

alternatives.option: Bundle ProjectGraphRecorder and ContextDiscoveryRecorder into one constructor argument.
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-177 keeps them as separate ports for narrow capability. The host happens to bind both to the same DreamGraph adapter instance, but the orchestrator and the assembler still see two separate port surfaces.

expected: The v10.0.0 cutover commit's diff in extension.ts is a one-line swap: from the v1 entry point to `await createArchitectHost({...}).runPass(...)`.
Future port additions only touch host/index.ts and the calling site, not extension.ts.
Sparse-mode is the *default* operating mode of the host — omit the McpClient and the orchestrator still produces complete passes against fallback signals.
Provider window changes (new flagship model, lock bump) flow through resolveDefaultModel automatically without touching any builder/composer code.
risks: Adapter wiring drift: a new port added later may be forgotten in createArchitectHost. Mitigation: OrchestratorPorts is the canonical aggregate; TypeScript fails the build if a slot is missing.
windowTokensOverride misused in production. Mitigation: documented as test/degradation-only; default path always resolves from the provider profile.
Same adapter satisfying two ports could mask test failures (one port behaves but the other does not). Mitigation: the two recorder ports have different method shapes; the type system enforces both.

guard_rails: Test (8B): createArchitectHost({ providerId, executor: stubExecutor }) returns a working host that can run a pass producing a non-empty PassResult with sections.length === 0 and unmetRequirements.length === manifest.requirements.length.
Test (8B): host.windowTokens === resolveDefaultModel(providerId).model.contextWindow when no override given.
Test (8B): host wired with an InMemoryKeyValueStore + InMemoryMcpClient survives load/save round-trips (saveTaskState then loadTaskState returns deep-equal state).
Build-time check (Slice 8B): grep that fails if host/index.ts imports from /^(vscode|fs|node:|http|mcp_)/ or from any v1 path.

decisions.title: Provider/model agnosticity: every user-facing fix is applied at provider-neutral seams

context.problem: A defect that manifests under one provider/model can tempt a fix inside that provider's adapter. Such adapter-local fixes silently diverge user-facing behavior across providers, recur the moment another provider's model exhibits the same pattern, and violate ADR-148's no-branch-on-provider principle. Context: during the v10.0.0 Lattice cutover smoke test of architect-v2, the chat surface leaked raw tool-envelope JSON into a chat bubble, and the same defect can be produced by any provider/model.
constraints: ADR-140 forbids v1 imports inside architect-v2.
ADR-160 keeps the card taxonomy closed.
ADR-148 pins provider-id branching out of the orchestrator.
The host->webview seam is the only channel through which provider output may reach the user, and only as typed messages.

decision.chosen: All user-facing fixes for architect-v2 MUST be applied at provider-neutral seams. (1) Free-text sanitization lives in cards/render.ts as sanitizeFreeText, invoked by renderTrailingNote and renderCompletion. (2) Folding model rationale into structured cards lives in orchestrator/loop.ts via composeTerminalSummary. (3) Live activity ticker events come from a thin ExecutorPort wrapper in host/index.ts that taps every executeCapability call. (4) Provider/model selection UI lives in host/chat-panel/ and reads provider metadata exclusively through providers/registry.ts; no UI code names a provider id. (5) Per-provider state is keyed by providerId but the storage shape is identical for every provider. (6) Adapter-only changes are restricted to wire-protocol concerns and to the static provider profile.

alternatives.option: Patch each adapter when its model misbehaves
alternatives.rejected_because: Defect recurs with any provider/model; multiplies code paths; violates ADR-148.

alternatives.option: Centralize sanitization in a shared adapter base class
alternatives.rejected_because: Sanitization is rendering, not transport. Bypasses host->webview seam.

alternatives.option: Add per-provider feature flags to gate UI behavior
alternatives.rejected_because: Combinatorial UI states; behavior depends on chosen model; violates the agnosticity goal.

expected: sanitizeFreeText, composeTerminalSummary, and the ExecutorPort activity wrap are part of architect-v2's shared seam contract.
Adapters stay narrow: pure wire concerns.
When a new provider is added, no UI/render/loop change is required.
User-visible behavior is byte-identical across providers given the same model output shape.
risks: Centralizing sanitization in cards/render.ts means a bug there affects every provider.
ExecutorPort wrap adds a thin layer of indirection on every capability call.
If a future provider returns structured fields the orchestrator does not yet split, the leak path reopens until the adapter is updated.

guard_rails: Do NOT add JSON-stripping, prose-cleanup, ticker-event emission, default-model selection, provider/model dropdown logic, or any user-visible policy inside an adapter file. Such code MUST live in cards/render.ts, orchestrator/loop.ts, host/index.ts wrapper layer, or host/chat-panel/.
Do NOT introduce branches on providerId outside of host/chat-panel/panel.ts settings persistence. Branch on model.capabilities.api or a provider-neutral capability flag.
Do NOT bypass the typed HostToWebview message seam. The webview MUST NOT receive any provider-shaped payload.
Do NOT key user-facing copy or behavior on provider displayName.

decisions.title: V1 hybrid chat panel is the canonical VS Code architect surface; architect-v2 remains quarantined

context.problem: The extension contains both the shipping V1 hybrid architect/chat surface and a retained architect-v2 prototype tree, creating risk that future changes may accidentally reactivate or split product behavior across competing orchestration paths.
constraints: The currently working Extension Host UI and command surface are wired through extension.ts, commands.ts, chat-panel.ts, architect-llm.ts, and context-builder.ts.
The codebase intentionally retains architect-v2 sources for historical reference.
Future contributors and agents need guard rails to avoid re-importing quarantined code without explicit review.

decision.chosen: Treat the V1 hybrid stack (ChatPanel + ArchitectLlm + ContextBuilder + autonomy loop + webview helpers) as the only canonical VS Code architect surface in v10.0.0. Keep architect-v2 quarantined as non-activated historical reference unless a new ADR explicitly replaces the canonical surface.

alternatives.option: Re-enable architect-v2 alongside V1
alternatives.rejected_because: Would fragment the UX, duplicate orchestration seams, and increase risk of drift between command, reporting, and continuation behavior.

alternatives.option: Delete architect-v2 immediately
alternatives.rejected_because: Historical reference and migration context are still useful, and current code comments intentionally preserve the tree without activating it.

expected: Future work should extend the V1 hybrid path rather than adding parallel activation paths.
Command and webview debugging can focus on ChatPanel and related V1 modules.
Quarantined prototype code remains available for reference without affecting runtime behavior.
risks: Contributors may still edit quarantined code assuming it is live.
The retained prototype tree can create cognitive overhead during code search.

guard_rails: Do NOT import or register architect-v2 modules from extension.ts without a new superseding ADR.
Do NOT add command palette or webview entry points that bypass ChatPanel as the canonical architect surface.
When documenting architect runtime behavior, anchor claims to extension.ts, chat-panel.ts, architect-llm.ts, and context-builder.ts unless a new ADR changes the seam.

decisions.title: Keep Architect core normalized while classifying MCP tools by authority

context.problem: CLI agents such as Codex CLI, Copilot CLI, and Claude CLI can be configured with MCP servers and generic/provider tools. Architect needs to use DreamGraph tools as authoritative system capabilities without letting provider-native inline tools or arbitrary MCP tools redefine Architect core contracts or become untrusted sources of truth.
constraints: Architect core may speak only ArchitectRunRequest, ArchitectRunResult, and ArchitectPassEnvelope.
Provider-specific requests, transcripts, process captures, MCP configs, and tool outputs must remain adapter-private until normalized.
DreamGraph tools may be exposed to CLI agents via MCP, but their outputs must still be policy-checked and normalized before Architect core consumes them.
Generic MCP tools and provider inline tools may be useful for context or local actions, but they must not be treated as authoritative DreamGraph facts unless revalidated by DreamGraph.

CLI implementations differ: Copilot CLI uses ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json and per-server tools allowlists; Codex CLI uses ~/.codex/config.toml / project config with mcp_servers allowlists, required flags, timeouts, and sandbox/approval controls; Claude CLI/Claude Code MCP support must be handled through its own adapter policy.

decision.chosen: Classify MCP/tool access into authority tiers. DreamGraph-authoritative MCP tools are the only tool outputs that can become authoritative Architect evidence, and only after adapter readiness checks, allowlist verification, transcript capture, and normalization into ArchitectRunResult. Generic MCP tools and provider inline tools are treated as contextual or action-producing provider-local capabilities; their outputs can be quoted in adapter evidence but cannot mutate Architect state or satisfy authoritative graph/tool requirements unless revalidated through DreamGraph. Architect core remains provider-agnostic and receives only ArchitectRunRequest, ArchitectRunResult, and ArchitectPassEnvelope.

alternatives.option: Let each CLI expose arbitrary MCP and inline tools directly to Architect core.
alternatives.rejected_because: This would couple Architect to provider-specific tool semantics and allow untrusted/generic tools to become de facto authoritative.

alternatives.option: Disable all MCP support for CLI agents.
alternatives.rejected_because: This wastes the strongest integration path for giving subscription/CLI agents controlled DreamGraph context and tool access.

alternatives.option: Treat all MCP servers equally if configured by the user.
alternatives.rejected_because: User configuration alone does not establish authority, provenance, normalization, or compatibility with Architect contracts.

expected: Adapters must generate or validate CLI-specific MCP configuration before authoritative runs.
Adapters must capture MCP/tool transcripts sufficient for audit and normalization.
Routing can fail closed when an authoritative DreamGraph operation is requested but the CLI adapter cannot prove DreamGraph MCP tools are available under policy.
Provider inline tools remain useful but are never considered a substitute for DreamGraph-authoritative MCP tools.
The same ArchitectRunResult contract can represent manual bridge, CLI, and API outputs without changing Architect core.
risks: CLI MCP configuration formats and flags may change across versions.
Some CLIs may not support run-scoped MCP config cleanly, requiring profile isolation or temporary config directories.
Generic MCP/tool output can still influence model text unless prompts and adapters label authority boundaries clearly.
Provider CLIs may auto-select tools, making strict transcript capture and tool allowlists important.

guard_rails: Do not add provider-specific request/result types to Architect core.
Do not treat generic MCP or provider inline tool output as authoritative DreamGraph facts without revalidation.
Do not route authoritative Architect operations to a CLI adapter unless DreamGraph MCP readiness and allowlists pass.
Keep CLI process captures, MCP configs, and provider-native transcripts adapter-private except as normalized evidence fields in ArchitectRunResult.
Prefer fail-closed behavior for missing or ambiguous MCP authority configuration.

decisions.title: Provider-neutral workspace snapshot tracking for pending change review

context.problem: The Copilot-style pending diff Keep/Undo UI is provider-neutral, but opaque write tools can mutate workspace files without calling ChangeReviewService per-file hooks, leaving no pending reviews to render.
constraints: Do not tie review tracking to Copilot-specific adapters or providers.
Cover local, MCP/daemon, and future tool execution paths from a common boundary.
Avoid noisy/generated files by reusing existing reviewable-file filtering.
Preserve explicit per-file tracking paths that already exist.
Keep the first implementation simple enough to patch at the known chat-panel tool execution loop.
related_tensions: provider-neutral UI vs provider-specific write paths
opaque tool side effects vs explicit file-level write APIs

decision.chosen: Add provider-neutral workspace snapshot support to ChangeReviewService and wrap classified write tool execution in the common chat-panel tool loop. Before an isWriteToolName-classified tool runs, snapshot reviewable workspace files; after the tool finishes, detect changed/created/deleted files, register pending reviews, and post pending reviews to the UI.

alternatives.option: Wrap Copilot CLI HOST_FS/writeFile
alternatives.rejected_because: It would tie the feature to Copilot and miss MCP/local/future write paths.

alternatives.option: Only rely on local-tools explicit captureBeforeWrite/recordAfterWrite hooks
alternatives.rejected_because: Opaque daemon/MCP write tools bypass those hooks, so UI remains empty for common flows.

alternatives.option: Use VS Code file watchers only
alternatives.rejected_because: Watchers are asynchronous and harder to correlate with tool execution and before-content snapshots.

expected: Pending diff UI can be populated for any provider-neutral write tool path.
Existing local tool explicit hooks remain compatible.
Some write tools will incur bounded workspace scan overhead.
Future providers can benefit without adapter-specific code.
risks: Large workspaces may make full snapshots expensive.
If filtering is too broad, generated files may appear in pending reviews.
If filtering is too narrow, relevant edits may be missed.
Deleted-file handling must avoid crashing when after-content is unavailable.

guard_rails: Use ReviewableFileFilter when selecting snapshot candidates.
Only run snapshots for tools classified by isWriteToolName.
Keep Copilot-specific adapters unchanged.
Post pending reviews after write tool execution completes.
Preserve captureBeforeWrite/recordAfterWrite APIs for explicit paths.

decisions.title: Provider-safe plugin tool names and native-source discovery

context.problem: Dotted plugin tool names such as examples.hello-events.greet can pass DreamGraph plugin gates but are rejected by LLM providers that require tool names to match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$. Separately, bootstrap/scan can no-op on C/C++ projects because native source extensions are absent from scanner extension allow-lists.
constraints: Provider-facing tool names must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ and therefore cannot contain dots.
Plugin contribution gates must reject invalid tool names before tools enter MCP/provider catalogs.
The rule must be applied consistently in daemon manager, host gates, SDK manifest validation, and examples/tests.
Scanner discovery must include common C/C++ source/header extensions without weakening existing language support.
related_tensions: Plugin IDs often use reverse-DNS/dotted naming while provider tool identifiers forbid dots.
Backward compatibility with old <plugin-id>.<tool> names conflicts with provider-safe registration.
Language-specific scan allow-lists can silently exclude valid target projects.

decision.chosen: Use provider-safe plugin tool identifiers at the plugin boundary: derive plugin prefixes by replacing non [a-zA-Z0-9_-] characters with underscores and require every registered tool name to match the provider-safe pattern. Add C/C++ source and header extensions to scan/bootstrap allow-lists.

alternatives.option: Sanitize tool names only immediately before provider calls
alternatives.rejected_because: It creates mismatches between plugin manifests, host gates, MCP catalogs, and execution dispatch.

alternatives.option: Continue accepting dotted plugin names internally
alternatives.rejected_because: Invalid names can still leak into provider tool catalogs and break assistant requests before execution.

alternatives.option: Rely on manual target overrides for C++ projects
alternatives.rejected_because: Bootstrap/scan should work for common C++ repositories without requiring users to know internal extension filters.

expected: Invalid dotted plugin tool names are rejected early with actionable errors.
Provider tool registration no longer fails due to plugin-contributed dotted names.
Plugin authors use sanitized prefixes such as examples_hello-events_greet or examples_hello_events_greet instead of examples.hello-events.greet.
OpenRCT2-style C/C++ projects are discoverable by default during scan/bootstrap.
risks: Existing plugins using old dotted tool names must update manifests.
If execution dispatch assumes dotted names elsewhere, those call paths must be migrated to sanitized names.
Naive extension expansion may increase scan volume on large native repositories.

guard_rails: Add or keep tests asserting no registered/contributed tool name contains dots or violates ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$.
Keep plugin-id to tool-prefix derivation deterministic and shared between host/daemon validation paths.
Run targeted plugin gate/manifest tests plus build after patching.
If scan volume becomes excessive, add explicit caps or ignore rules rather than removing C++ extension support.

decisions.title: Copilot CLI adapter uses bounded prompt-file context injection

context.problem: The Copilot CLI adapter must pass DreamGraph Architect context to a subscription CLI without overflowing command-line limits or letting provider-specific prompt assembly leak into Architect core. Earlier file-level ADR exports were not accurate enough for this adapter-specific context-economy decision.
constraints: Architect core remains normalized around ArchitectRunRequest, ArchitectRunResult, and ArchitectPassEnvelope; Copilot-specific prompt serialization is adapter-private.
The CLI invocation must stay reliable on Windows and other shells with finite argv length limits.
Prompt construction must preserve the current-turn marker contract and bounded chat history so the model responds only to the active user request while retaining enough prior context.
DreamGraph MCP grounding remains authoritative for repository facts; serialized prompt context is a transport envelope, not a replacement for MCP graph queries.
Prompt-size diagnostics must be observable through Context Inspector output.

decision.chosen: Keep Copilot CLI prompt composition inside the Copilot adapter/provider boundary, build the Architect envelope with context-economy controls, retain a bounded history window, mark the current turn explicitly, and fall back to a temporary prompt.md file when the serialized prompt exceeds the safe argv byte budget. Surface prompt byte count, history count, advertised MCP server/tool count, current-turn marker status, and model selection to the Context Inspector.

alternatives.option: Pass the full prompt exclusively through argv
alternatives.rejected_because: Large Architect prompts can exceed shell or process argument limits, especially on Windows, and fail before Copilot CLI starts.

alternatives.option: Move Copilot prompt serialization into Architect core
alternatives.rejected_because: That would contaminate provider-neutral core contracts with a provider-specific CLI transport concern.

alternatives.option: Rely only on MCP tools and omit serialized task/history context
alternatives.rejected_because: The CLI still needs the concrete current turn, autonomy/reporting contracts, and bounded conversation context before it can decide which MCP tools to call.

expected: Copilot CLI runs remain reliable for large Architect prompts by using prompt.md file fallback above the adapter's argv budget.
Context Inspector can explain why a run used a file-backed prompt and how much context was serialized.
Architect core remains provider-neutral while Copilot-specific transport policy stays adapter-local.
The current-turn marker and bounded history reduce stale-context responses and prompt bloat.
risks: Prompt file lifecycle bugs could leave stale temporary prompt artifacts or point a run at the wrong content.
A provider CLI change in accepted prompt-file invocation semantics could require adapter updates.
Plain byte-count logging is less structured than shared budget-component telemetry unless separately integrated with BudgetCoordinator summaries.

guard_rails: Do not move Copilot CLI prompt serialization or prompt.md fallback into provider-neutral Architect core.
Do not remove the explicit current-turn marker from Copilot CLI prompts without replacing it with an equally strong active-turn isolation mechanism.
Do not disable bounded history or argv byte budgeting for Copilot CLI runs.
Do not treat serialized prompt context as authoritative graph truth; repository facts still require DreamGraph MCP grounding.

decisions.title: Copilot CLI live output is sourced from NDJSON event stream

context.problem: The Copilot CLI adapter needs reliable live assistant text, reasoning, and tool-call telemetry in the VS Code chat UI. File-based or audit-tail derived observations are insufficient as the primary runtime source because they can lag, miss provider events, or duplicate transcript content.
constraints: Copilot CLI exposes typed stdout events when invoked with --output-format json.
The adapter must preserve provider-neutral chat/tool trace contracts while keeping Copilot-specific event shapes adapter-local.
Assistant text must not be duplicated by combining streamed deltas with a later full transcript chunk.
Tool start/complete events must map into ToolTraceEntry rows with stable provenance such as dreamgraph:<tool> or cli:<tool>.
Audit-live tailing may remain as secondary MCP provenance but must not compete with the CLI stdout event stream as the authoritative live UX source.

decision.chosen: Invoke Copilot CLI with --output-format json and treat its stdout NDJSON event stream as the authoritative live runtime feed for assistant message deltas, reasoning deltas, tool execution start/complete events, and final result metadata. Parse events in the Copilot adapter, translate them through provider-port into provider-neutral chat events and ToolTraceEntry updates, and suppress duplicate full-transcript emission when per-token assistant deltas were already streamed.

alternatives.option: Use only the final CLI transcript after process exit
alternatives.rejected_because: The UI would lose live tool-call and token streaming behavior and would provide poorer progress visibility.

alternatives.option: Use bridge audit-live tailing as the primary source
alternatives.rejected_because: Audit tailing is MCP-specific secondary provenance and can lag or diverge from the provider CLI's own typed runtime events.

alternatives.option: Expose Copilot CLI raw event types directly to Architect core and chat UI
alternatives.rejected_because: That would couple provider-neutral components to Copilot-specific event schemas instead of normalizing at the adapter boundary.

expected: Users see live assistant text/reasoning and tool progress during Copilot CLI runs.
Tool trace rows are populated from the CLI's own typed runtime events rather than inferred after the fact.
Provider-specific NDJSON parsing remains isolated in the Copilot CLI adapter and provider port.
Duplicate assistant messages are avoided when streamed deltas already cover the final response.
risks: Copilot CLI may change its output-format json event schema or event names.
Malformed or partial NDJSON lines can reduce live trace fidelity even if the final CLI result succeeds.
Provider event timing might still differ from MCP audit persistence timing, requiring clear provenance labeling.

guard_rails: Do not replace the Copilot CLI NDJSON stdout stream with bridge audit-live tailing as the primary live UX source without a new ADR.
Do not pass raw Copilot CLI event objects into Architect core; normalize them at the adapter/provider-port boundary.
Do not emit a full transcript chunk when assistant.message_delta events already streamed the same content.
Keep tool start/complete translation explicit so Context Inspector/chat traces retain tool provenance.

decisions.title: Copilot CLI Context Inspector records adapter prompt composition

context.problem: Operators need to understand what the Copilot CLI adapter actually sent to the provider and which DreamGraph MCP surface was advertised, especially because repository markdown ADR files were not accurate for the live DreamGraph ADR state. Without adapter-level Context Inspector output, prompt economy and MCP bridging failures are hard to diagnose.
constraints: Context Inspector output must be compact enough for routine use but specific enough to diagnose prompt byte size, history volume, MCP advertisement, current-turn isolation, and selected model.
Diagnostics must not expose secrets or raw full prompt content.
The adapter must report facts from the actual prompt-composition path rather than stale documentation files.
BudgetCoordinator structured accounting and Context Inspector plain-line diagnostics may coexist, but they should not contradict each other.
Provider-specific diagnostic fields must remain behind the adapter/provider boundary unless normalized for shared UI display.

decision.chosen: Emit Copilot CLI prompt-composition diagnostics to the Context Inspector when the adapter composes a run: serialized prompt byte length, bounded history message count, advertised MCP server name and tool count, current-turn marker status, and model selection. Treat this as adapter provenance for live run diagnosis, while preserving the opportunity to add structured BudgetCoordinator prompt-component accounting separately.

alternatives.option: Do not log Copilot CLI prompt composition
alternatives.rejected_because: Users and maintainers would have no compact evidence of context-economy behavior or MCP bridge advertisement during a run.

alternatives.option: Dump the full serialized prompt into Context Inspector
alternatives.rejected_because: That would violate context economy, risk exposing sensitive conversation/source content, and make the inspector noisy.

alternatives.option: Depend on markdown ADR/docs files for Copilot adapter truth
alternatives.rejected_because: The user explicitly identified those files as inaccurate for DreamGraph ADR state; the live graph and runtime inspector must be treated as the authoritative surfaces.

expected: Copilot CLI runs expose compact diagnostics for prompt size, bounded history, MCP advertisement, current-turn isolation, and model selection.
MCP bridge failures such as missing dreamgraph command/tool advertisement can be diagnosed from live run metadata.
Context Inspector remains a low-noise operational surface rather than a raw prompt dump.
Future work can align this plain diagnostic line with shared structured budget summaries without changing the adapter decision.
risks: Plain text inspector lines are less queryable than structured budget records.
If prompt-composition metadata diverges from BudgetCoordinator component accounting, operators may see inconsistent budget narratives.
Overly detailed diagnostics could accidentally expose provider or workspace internals if expanded without review.

guard_rails: Do not remove Copilot CLI prompt-composition diagnostics from Context Inspector without replacing them with an equally visible structured diagnostic.
Do not log full serialized prompts, secrets, MCP config contents, or raw tool payloads in this inspector line.
Do not rely on repository markdown ADR exports as the source of truth for Copilot adapter decisions; use live DreamGraph ADR records.
Keep provider-specific diagnostic collection adapter-local and expose only normalized/compact facts to shared UI surfaces.

decisions.title: Copilot CLI is a native DreamGraph Architect adapter

context.problem: Copilot CLI integration has moved from a dumb provider subprocess bridge to a DreamGraph-native Architect adapter. The architecture needs to preserve this as a first-class adapter decision and make the reusable pattern available for future CLI adapters such as Codex CLI without copying provider-specific implementation details into Architect core.
constraints: Architect core must remain provider-neutral and continue to exchange normalized ArchitectRunRequest, ArchitectRunResult, and ArchitectPassEnvelope contracts.
DreamGraph MCP grounding remains the authoritative source for repository facts and graph operations during Copilot CLI runs.
Copilot-specific prompt composition, MCP bridge readiness, event parsing, and process behavior must stay inside the Copilot CLI adapter/provider boundary.
The adapter must preserve context economy controls, current-turn isolation, live tool trace normalization, and Context Inspector diagnostics.
Future Codex CLI reuse should extract principles and shared adapter seams, not blindly clone Copilot CLI provider details.

decision.chosen: Treat Copilot CLI as a native DreamGraph Architect adapter: it participates in graph-grounded runs, bounded context assembly, DreamGraph MCP authority checks, normalized live event/tool-trace streaming, prompt-file fallback, and Context Inspector observability while keeping provider-specific mechanics adapter-local. Use this adapter as the reference pattern for a future Codex CLI native adapter, reusing the architecture principles and shared seams while respecting Codex-specific CLI configuration, sandboxing, event, and MCP behavior.

alternatives.option: Keep Copilot CLI as a dumb subprocess bridge with only prompt-in/text-out behavior
alternatives.rejected_because: That would lose DreamGraph authority semantics, context-economy enforcement, MCP readiness checks, live tool traces, and inspectable adapter provenance.

alternatives.option: Move Copilot CLI behavior into Architect core
alternatives.rejected_because: That would contaminate provider-neutral Architect contracts with provider-specific CLI transport, prompt, and event-stream details.

alternatives.option: Clone Copilot CLI implementation directly for Codex CLI
alternatives.rejected_because: Codex CLI has different configuration, sandbox/approval, and event semantics; only the native-adapter principles and normalized seams should be reused.

expected: Copilot CLI is treated as a first-class DreamGraph Architect execution path rather than a generic CLI wrapper.
Graph-grounded answers can fail closed when DreamGraph MCP bridging is unavailable or untrusted.
Live Copilot CLI output remains observable through normalized chat/tool trace surfaces and compact Context Inspector diagnostics.
The Codex CLI adapter can follow the same native-adapter principle with lower architectural risk, while adapting to Codex-specific runtime semantics.
Architect core remains clean because provider-specific logic stays behind adapter/provider boundaries.
risks: Future Copilot CLI output, MCP, or prompt-file behavior may change and require adapter updates.
Reference reuse for Codex CLI may accidentally overfit to Copilot-specific assumptions if not reviewed against Codex behavior.
